bibliography.checked_against: Crossref (doi:10.1002/lno.10148) and the article's first page
bibliography.corrections: Verified citation (the work exists as the brief recalled it): Beyene, M. T. & Jain, S. 2015. Wintertime weather-climate variability and its links to early spring ice-out in Maine lakes. Limnology and Oceanography 60(6): 1890-1905. doi:10.1002/lno.10148. (Online 4 September 2015; issue dated November 2015. The UMaine repository record gives the issue's page range 1855-2235 by mistake; the article is 1890-1905.)
bibliography.note: the brief's 'Maine lake ice-out and climate' is right in substance, but the paper is about interannual drivers (winter degree-days, TNH and NAO teleconnections) of early ice-out, not chiefly about the long-term trend

claims.claim: Maine lakes have recently had their earliest ice-out dates on record (in over a century)
claims.quote: Maine lakes have recorded their earliest ice-out dates in over a century
claims.conditions: the spring of 2010 (citing a Bangor Daily News report, Bayly 2010); the study's own record is eight lakes, 1950-2010

claims.claim: the trend in Maine ice-out dates is toward earlier ice-out
claims.location: p. 1890 (PDF p. 2), introduction; p. 1895 (PDF p. 7), Results
claims.quote: only modest monotonic trends towards early ice-out are observed
claims.conditions: qualitative; the authors attribute the trend analysis to Hodgkins et al. (2002), noting that 'recent decades show appreciable change' in decadal smoothing, with spring ice-out changes corresponding to a 1.4-1.5 °C rise in March-April temperature over 150 years in New England
claims.note: direction only; see the next two claims for what the paper's own data show

claims.claim: a rate of change of Maine ice-out (days per decade)
claims.note: the paper gives no rate. Its own principal-component series for the eight lakes (1950-2010) has no secular trend ('no secular trend for PC1 time series was found', p. 1895, Supporting Information Table B6); it describes instead a run of late ice-outs in the 1960s-70s overtaken by early ones since the early 1980s. For a rate cite Hodgkins et al. 2002 (Int. J. Climatol. 22: 1819-1827, doi:10.1002/joc.857, per this paper's references) or Hodgkins 2013, which §3.1.4 already uses

claims.claim: early ice-outs cluster in recent decades
claims.location: p. 1895 (PDF p. 7), 'Statistics of early/late ice-out events in Maine' and Fig. 1
claims.quote: approximately 75% of the earliest ice-out years occurred after the 1970s
claims.conditions: the ten earliest ice-out years of each of eight lakes (China, Damariscotta, Maranacook, Moosehead, Mooselookmeguntic, Rangeley, Sebec, West Grand), 1950-2010; also 39 of the 80 earliest-ten events fell in the last 15 years (1996-2010), the 97th percentile of random 15-year windows, and only 10 of the 80 latest-ten events

claims.claim: spring air temperature explains most of the year-to-year variation in Maine ice-out, winter temperature a smaller part
claims.location: p. 1900 (PDF p. 12), Discussion item 1; p. 1897 (PDF p. 9), Results
claims.quote: temperatures accounts for more than half
claims.conditions: spring = March-April air temperature at USHCN stations, > 50 % of the variance of ice-out (p < 0.05); winter (January-February) accumulated freezing degree-days explain 15-20 % and melting degree-days 10-28 %; ice-out is more sensitive to warm winters (low AFDD, high AMDD) than to cold ones
claims.note: matches §3.1.4's 'March-April air temperature explaining about half its year-to-year variance' (there credited to Hodgkins, James & Huntington 2005)

notes: Useful for §3.1.4: West Grand Lake (the paper's nearest long ice record) is one of the eight lakes. Data: ice-out from Hodgkins 2010 (USGS OFR 2010-1214) and the Maine Department of Conservation; temperatures from six USHCN stations. Other findings: strongly negative winter TNH phases, and to a lesser extent positive NAO phases, go with early ice-out; in 1983 (strong El Nino) Sebec Lake's winter was 2.5 °C warm and ice-out 9 days early (p. 1891). Ice cover usually disappears in April-May. The peer-reviewed form of the Hodgkins, James & Huntington work that §3.1.4 cites as a 2005 USGS Fact Sheet is, per this paper's references, Int. J. Climatol. 22: 1819-1827 (2002).
